lines: Dig a hole in your backyard and climb in. Is that a bunker? Not even close. Here's what it takes.
Problem one: the walls cave in. One cubic yard of soil can weigh as much as a car. Fix: a box of steel rebar and poured concrete.
Problem two: water seeps into every crack. Fix: a waterproof membrane on the outside, and a drain pipe in gravel that carries it away.
Problem three: air. Body heat and stale air build up fast. Fix: two pipes. Fresh air comes in through a filter, stale air goes out.
Problem four: radiation. Fix: bury it. Every nine centimeters of packed earth cuts gamma rays in half. Ninety centimeters cuts them a thousand times.
Problem five: the door. Gamma rays travel in straight lines, like light. Fix: an entrance that turns a corner, under a steel hatch.
Every layer has one job. Concrete holds back the soil, the membrane keeps it dry, the pipes bring air, and the earth is the shield.
From the garden, you'd only see a hatch and two pipes. Below, three feet of dirt block over ninety nine point nine percent of the radiation.
